title: AAP discovery document (broker profile, sections 8.5.1 and 8.5.2)
description: The JSON object an operator serves at `/.well-known/aap` on its own origin (broker profile section 8.5.1). The five broker members (`aapVersions`, `signatureSuites`, `authorizationDetailsTypes`, `presentationBindings`, `jwks`) are present when the operator runs a broker, and then all five are present: `dependentRequired` makes each require the other four. A document holds the five broker members, `browserSession` (broker profile section 8.5.2), or both; a document that holds only `browserSession` is valid. `acceptedIssuers` and `delegationPath` sit at the top level because a counterparty of the broker and a browser-side consumer both read them. A reader ignores a member it does not know, as broker profile section 8.3 has a verifier ignore an unknown optional claim, so the schema allows unknown members at every level. No member the schema defines carries text for a reader to display. The `not` keyword beside the pattern of each `authorizationDetailsTypes` item rejects a line break, as in the CGT claim schema: under Python's `re.search`, which the jsonschema package uses, `$` also matches before a final line break. The other patterns end without `$` and reject a line break through their own `not` keyword.

aapVersions.description: The AAP protocol versions the broker supports, for the negotiation of broker profile section 8.1.

signatureSuites.description: The signature suites the broker supports, each the JOSE `alg` value of a row of the suite registry of AAP-SPEC section 9.5 (`EdDSA`, `ML-DSA-65`). A reader ignores a value it does not know.

authorizationDetailsTypes.description: The set of `authorization_details` entry types the broker understands, with the semantics of RFC 9396 section 10 `authorization_details_types_supported`. Each value is the registry URI of AAP-SPEC section 4.4.1, the wire value of an entry's `type`, under the pattern the CGT claim schema gives that `type`. The producer rule of AAP-SPEC section 4.4 reads this member. An empty array says that the broker understands no entry type.

presentationBindings.description: The presentation bindings of broker profile section 8.5 that the broker accepts: `http` (the `Agent-Trust-Credential` header), `a2a-agent-card` and `mcp-manifest`. A reader ignores a value it does not know.

jwks.description: Static public key material for the broker-assertion signing key: a JWK Set (RFC 7517 section 5). Each key carries `kid`, the value the protected header of a broker assertion names (AAP-SPEC section 9.2). A key that carries a private or symmetric key member (`d`, `p`, `q`, `dp`, `dq`, `qi`, `oth`, `k`, `priv`) is rejected.

acceptedIssuers.description: The DIDs of the credential issuers whose credentials the operator, as relying party, accepts. Each value is a DID: `did:`, a method name of lowercase letters and digits, a colon, and an identifier in the characters of a DID (letters, digits, `.`, `-`, `_`, `%` and `:`, with `/` for the resource identifiers of the did:opena2a method). A web address, a name and a DID URL with a query or a fragment are rejected. A consumer never holds fewer requests, and never lets a held request go, because of this member.

delegationPath.description: The path, on the origin that serves the document, where an agent obtains delegated authority from the operator in place of acting in a customer's signed-in session. A path of at most 255 characters that starts with a single `/`. A value that starts with `//`, or that holds a backslash, a space or a control character, is rejected: a URL parser reads a backslash as `/` and removes a tab or a line break, so either can turn the value into one that starts with `//` and names another origin. A reader resolves the value against the document's origin and drops it unless the result has that origin (broker profile section 8.5.2).

browserSession.description: The browser session member (broker profile section 8.5.2): the requests to the origin that serves the document which a browser-side consumer holds when an agent makes them in a customer's signed-in session. The member only restricts: a consumer never holds fewer requests, and never lets a held request go, because of it.

profile.description: The version of the browser session profile. A value other than "1" fails validation, so a consumer that knows only this version treats a later one as a member that fails validation (broker profile section 8.5.2).

pathPrefix.description: A literal path that starts with `/`, at most 255 characters, holding none of `*`, `^`, `|`, `?`, `#` and backslash, and no space or control character, so a consumer can match it as a literal prefix.

category.description: What kind of request the entry holds. A consumer describes a held request in its own words from this value.
